wiki/allostasis.title: Allostasis
wiki/allostasis.content:
Overview
Allostasis is the active process through which the body anticipates changes and adjusts itself in an effort to maintain stability. As the body undergoes perceived changes in its environment, the brain constantly adjusts hormones, neurotransmitters, and signals throughout the nervous system. For instance, when exercising or physically working, the body raises its blood pressure to ensure it can keep up with the increased pace of activity.
When someone uses substances, the brain experiences a spike in dopamine and other neurotransmitters that are countered with chemicals like corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) to protect oneself from overstimulation. In brief intermittent uses, this means the body eventually returns to a baseline, but chronic usage can permanently lower the baseline such that substances are used to alleviate a low mood rather than achieve a high mood. Allostasis describes the process through which these internal parameters are adjusted by the body in response to exposure from the environment, and the term “allostatic load” is used to describe the long-term effects on the body from these changes.
History and Etymologu
The origin of the concept of allostasis is closely tied to community-level health observations that found stressful events correlated heavily with chronic health issues developing later in life. While we might take this for granted, it was often thought prior to Peter Sterling and Joseph Eyer’s work that a reduced mortality rate when young would correlate with more chronic diseases later in life. Instead, Sterling and Eyer found that groups experiencing the most social disruption, such as unemployed Americans struggling with financial instability and African-Americans struggling with the interpersonal and systemic impacts of racism, were also the most likely to develop hypertension. Previously this was hypothesized to be a result of genetic predisposition, but Sterling and Eyer countered with a mind-brain-body model that connected external stressors to internal physiological changes and long-term health consequences. The model of homeostasis didn’t explain why blood pressure didn’t return to a normal state after fluctuations throughout the day and instead responded primarily to the presence or absence of stressors. Chronic stress could also lead to long-term changes in blood pressure, suggesting a form of adaptation and self-regulation that the idea of a steady baseline the body seeks a return to can’t explain. The cumulative damage incurred by a body under chronic stress is often called an “allostatic load.”

wiki/allostatic-load.title: Allostatic Load
wiki/allostatic-load.content:
Overview
“Allostatic load” refers to the cumulative damage the body experiences as a result of chronic stress, often measured by blood pressure, cortisol levels, cholesterol, blood sugar, and inflammation. These can manifest in everyday life as increased symptoms of anxiety or depression, higher risk of heart disease and diabetes, and persistent fatigue.
Substance use disorders come with intense allostatic loads that can lower the baseline ability to receive pleasure from daily activities as the brain repeatedly tries to counteract overstimulation by releasing chemicals that can depress moods. Instead of using substances to achieve a high or a euphoria, someone might begin using substances just to feel their earlier baseline rather than

wiki/ambivalence.title: Ambivalence
wiki/ambivalence.content:
Overview
Ambivalence refers to the state of holding mixed feelings or thoughts, though it is often incorrectly used to mean “indifferent” rather than “conflicted.” For instance, one might really love their family but also experience a lot of stress talking to them, which means that the idea of interacting with them can feel conflicting. Another common example is wanting to quit a job that feels unbearable but also finding the financial instability of unemployment unbearable.

wiki/american-heart-association.title: American Heart Association (AHA)
wiki/american-heart-association.content:
Overview
The American Heart Association (AHA) is a nonprofit dedicated to reducing the effects of cardiovascular disease and stroke through funding research, educating the public on healthy living, and standardizing accessible cardiac care. 1
Research published by the AHA shows that deaths from heart disease directly related to substance use have risen by an average of 4% per year between 1999 and 2019. 2 They recommend against drinking alcohol for any potential benefits, with heavy drinking being a leading cause of hypertension, stroke, arrhythmias, and alcoholic cardiomyopathy. They’ve also called cocaine “the perfect heart attack drug” because it spikes blood pressure, influences the heart’s electrical system, and causes fatal arrhythmias by increasing oxygen demand while constricting blood vessels. Intravenous (IV) drug use can also introduce infections into the body that damage heart valves. The AHA actively advocates for equal treatment of those who struggle with substance use disorders, as many providers will discriminate against those with a history of substance use and even deny care. With the increasing concern in recent decades about opioid overdoses, the AHA educates the public and healthcare workforce about administering Naloxone (Narcan) in between cycles of CPR.

wiki/american-made.content:
Overview
American Made (2017) is a film adaptation of the life of Barry Seal, an airline pilot who smuggled drugs for the Medellin Cartel before becoming an informant for the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). His life and operations were used as inspiration in many action and thriller stories that center conspiracies involving US intelligence agencies, cartel trafficking, and Cold War politics. Though the movie is one of these and uses Seal’s name, the director Doug Liman has described it as “a fun lie based on a true story” since it mixes up timelines and creates a sympathetic protagonist out of Seal, who was a seasoned criminal rather than a bored and simple family man.

wiki/american-mental-wellness-associatio.title: American Mental Wellness Association (AMWA)
wiki/american-mental-wellness-associatio.content:
Overview
The American Mental Wellness Association (AMWA) is a national non-profit dedicated to raising awareness and supporting programs for mental wellness. One of their key arguments is that substance use is often motivated by the self-medication of disorders that can be screened for and stabilized early. They provide resources for education, prevention, early detection, early intervention, and research initiatives:


a proprietary questionnaire adapted from the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Test (MMPI), which flags shifts in behavior or psychological state before they lead to crises


8-hour certification courses for evidence-based Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) training


Girl Scout Patch Program as a specialized curriculum to cultivate emotional intelligence and self-care in young girls


educational toolkits and children’s books, like “Understanding Your Anxiety for Elementary Children”


rapid response strategy plans, which outline community interventions that address gaps in local mental health care

wiki/american-psychological-association.title: American Psychological Association (APA)
wiki/american-psychological-association.content:
Overview
With over 190,000 members, the American Psychological Association (APA) is the largest psychology association in the world.
Students who grew up in the American education system are likely to have been taught about the MLA style guide for formatting writing. The APA style guide is an alternative that many students see but haven’t been introduced to unless they spend time specifically exploring social science literature.
Commentary
As a result of being the largest psychology association in the world, the APA has sociopolitical significance that regularly leads to controversy and public scrutiny.
The Resignation of Christopher J. Ferguson
In 2021, Christopher J. Ferguson wrote an open letter to the American Psychological Association that he “cannot in good ethical conscience continue” membership as he feels “the APA has lots its way as either a science organization or an organization representing good clinical practice.”
Keep in mind that the APA President in 1946, Henry E. Garrett, was a rabid racist and eugenicist. He gave testimony in favor of school segregation in a case that was combined into Brown v. Board (1954), claiming that desegregation would bring “total demoralization and then disorganization in that order.” The Univerity of Virginia brought him on as a visiting professor in the Department of Education in 1955. In 1961, he published “The Equalitarian Dogma” where he argued “Blacks” were biologically intellectually inferior to “Whites.” In 1968, he wrote “Despite glamorized accounts to the contrary, the history of Black Africa over the past 5,000 years is largely a blank” and “The crime record of the Negro in the United States is little short of scandalous.” He would go on to accuse Jews and Jewish organizations of spreading the dogma, and in 1972 became Director of the Pioneer Fund, an organization inspired by the leading Nazi eugenicists behind the Nuremberg Laws. The American Psychological Association openly acknowledges the eugenicsts existed within their ranks existed into the 1980s. The 1997 winner of the Gold Medal Award for Life Achievement in Psychological Science, Raymond Cattell, supported eugenics and publicly acknowledged neo-Nazis and white supremacists so much so that the backlash to the announcement led to his withdrawal.
So surely, Ferguson must be objecting to the slow pace at which the APA prunes its ranks of pseudoscientific and harmful ideas right? No. The opposite actually.
Ferguson’s first complaints are about the APA distorting evidence on violent video games, spanking, and “guidelines for Men and Boys” that are “disparaging more traditional men.” He does not elaborate on what any of this means; one might reasonably speculate that this is just prefacing the discussion about race with a layer of other objections to imply that he’s spotted a constellation of issues.
On discussions of racism, his argument is that “adopting a dystopian and data-deficient view of the present is likely to do more harm than good.” Don’t let the expert credentials and clinical tone fool you, this is simply rehashing the standard “victim mentality” rhetoric used to dismiss the prevalence of racism by relocating the issue to internalized hysteria. The decline of explicit or implicit racism on average in no way suggests that existing discussion of racism is somehow fearmongering over a fantasized dystopia. Just because the average person on the street is less likely to think racial slurs when they see someone of a different race or would vote for Barack Obama over McCain and Romney doesn’t mean that racism has disappeared in other aspects of society.
Studies have repeatedly shown no statistically detectable decline in anti-Black hiring discrimination since 1989, with a 2017 meta-analysis by Lincoln Quillian showing that White applicants received 36% more callbacks than equally qualified Black applicants. A 2024 study by Josh Leung-Gagne reveals that the deadliest local police departments kill almost 7 times more frequently than the least deadly departments. Police violence is the 6th leading cause of death for men ages 25 to 29, with Black Americans almost three times as likely to be killed than White Americans. These trends can also be found in Native American and Latino communities. Further, a 2021 study published in The Lancet estimates that over half the deaths from police violence were either unreported or misclassified in the National Vital Statistics System used by the Center for Disease Control and Prevention.
Ferguson’s only discussion of this “complex and nuanced issue” is to accuse the APA of having a distorted perspective through the availability heuristic and social pressures that lead to an excessive focus on the murders of George Floyd and Ahmaud Arbery. Ironically, it’s Ferguson who has fixated on these cases while an absolute avalanche of evidence about the persistent effects of racism have been produced by his colleagues.
He also lazily brings up the claim that “evidence suggests class issues, rather than race, may predict negative outcomes” as if the preponderance of evidence doesn’t indicate both play a role. A 2024 study of the 100 largest US municipalities found that violent crime was mostly associated with income inequality and educational attainment rather than race, but a 2025 analysis of fatal shootings across >32,000 ZIP codes found that race remained an independent predictor after controlling for other factors.
Further, certain forms of racism have actually gotten worse over time. Anti-Asian hate crimes multiplied by a factor of nearly 5 from 2019 to 2021 following COVID-19, so Ferguson’s jab at the term “pandemic of racism” as a cliche is almost willfully ignorant of the long history of associating illness with “outsiders” and “foreigners”, or the Other. An NBER study found that even as public violence overall was declining, there was an observable increase in racially motivated violence against Asian Americans. Roughly one-third of Asian Americans reported experiencing some form of bias in the wake of the pandemic. FBI data shows that hate crimes in general increased 32% from 2019 to 2020, with anti-Black hate crimes increasing 49% and anti-Asian hate crimes increasing 77%. A recent 2026 paper by Manuel J Galvan et al. that models the distribution of racism finds that discriminatory effects are widespread rather than concentrated in just a few bad areas. Even though the total number of hate groups in the United States have been declining, the Southern Poverty Law Center identified that white-nationalist groups increased by 55% from 2017 to 2019.
And then, Ferguson drives his car right off the roads into the lake of culture wars, as he claims the APA “appears to sway with the political currents to what may be its optimal inward-focused gain at any given time. This appears to be as true regarding its historical involvement with the mistreatment of detainees as documented in the Hoffman Report as it is regarding its capitulation to ‘wokism’ in the present.”
The Hoffman Report was a 2015 analysis that found that leaders of the American Psychological Association had cooperated with the Department of Defense to develop ethical guidelines that allowed psychologists to participate in post-9/11 interrogations involving torture, euphemistically referred to as “enhanced interrogation techniques.” It is a Facebook-tier argument to suggest that the forces of “wokism” have the same influence on scientific institutions as the United States military. Remember that there is a long history of pseudoscientific eugenics tied to sociopolitical movements that Ferguson could have pointed to if he wanted to show the APA’s pattern of straying from science, but he chooses instead the comparison to the DoD that alludes to coercive and corrupt intentions.
It also seems Ferguson had no colleagues proofread this letter, as it is impossible to overlook that he says on one hand that “we also give extreme power to outrage and moral grandstanding as well as inaccurate sources of information such as anecdotes and ‘lived experiences’” while saying just one paragraph away that his opinion is “informed in part by my own time on the Council of Representatives, but also watching the APA’s public facing communications.” Outrage over ancedotes for me, but not for thee.
And of course, we can’t end one of these vague general complaints that everyone is talking too much about racism without a preemptive ad hominem defense that implies some maverick or underdog status: “I understand that my words will be unwelcome to the APA and perhaps many others aligned with this current movement on the sociopolitical left (and note, I identify as a liberal myself).”
Why shouldn’t they be unwelcome, when they rely on dystopian and data-deficient views of the present that is likely to do more harm than good? We would only be adhering to the standards Ferguson himself wishes the APA to adopt to keep out confirmation bias and cognitive dissonance driven by lived experiences.

The American Psychological Association No Longer Represents Good Science or Clinical Practice: An Open Letter on My Resignation from the APA

wiki/american-temperance-society.title: American Temperance Society
wiki/american-temperance-society.content:
Overview
The American Temperance Society (ATS), or the American Society for the Promotion of Temperance, was the first national social movement in the United States to mobilize support for social reforms. They started out in 1826 with Lyman Beecher and Justin Edwards leading a group opposed to the consumption of hard liquor, but eventually grew to favor the prohibition of all forms of alcohol through abstinence, or teetotalism. By 1835, their membership grew to 1.5 million people with more than 8000 local groups.
In 1836, in part to quell arguments from factions against total abstinence, the ATS merged into the American Temperance Union. The movement pushed for legal restrictions on alcohol consumption, like the 1851 Maine law. They were heavily disrupted by the American Civil War (1861-1865) and dissolved completely in 1866.

wiki/amnesia.title: Amnesia
wiki/amnesia.content:
Overview
Amnesia is a loss of memory or information connected to physical or psychological trauma. Contrary to stereotypical media portrayals of amnesia, it is not associated with a huge change in personality, identity, or intelligence. Amnesia tends to be categorized as either retrograde amnesia, meaning memory loss before the date of a traumatic event, or anterograde amnesia, meaning an inability to form new memories for long-term use. More specific labels can be used as well: transient global amnesia for a sudden onset of temporary memory loss, dissociative amnesia associated with stress and loss of personal information, childhood amnesia over recalling memories of early life (which isn’t uncommon), and post-traumatic amnesia after some kind of damaging neurological event leads to disorientation and confusion. It is also possible for someone to experience a combination of these or for amnesia to present in a complex form that operates at different layers.
Substance use can also trigger episodes of amnesia; drinking until blacked out is a form of drug-induced anterograde amnesia where someone might be awake and conscious with access to past memories but no ability to transform short-term memory into long-term memory. Blackouts are often described as either fragmentary blackouts with bits and pieces being remembered, in which case some people refer to them as “brownouts,” or en bloc blackouts where no memories at all are recorded over some period of time. This generally happens because substances like alcohol and marijuana directly impact the receptors in the hippocampus region of the brain, which plays a dominant role in filing memories into long-term storage. In severe cases of chronic substance use, permanent amnesia can set in through conditions like Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome which has a comparable memory loss pattern to dementia.
At the same time, people who suffer from dissociative amnesia after traumatic events can turn to substance use as a form of self-medication. Dissociative amnesia is thought to be a form of psychological self-defense in which the brain blocks out traumatic memories that are too overwhelming to process, but it doesn’t prevent the confusion or distress that arises from experiencing that dissociation. Amnesia in general weakens someone’s ability to recall information from the past that would be relevant for future choices, which can impact how individuals choose to use substances despite past consequences. The brain leans increasingly on unconscious and automated habits that can involve substance use.

wiki/amor-fati.title: Amor Fati
wiki/amor-fati.content:
Overview
“Amor fati” translates from Latin to “love of fate,” reflecting an attitude of embracing everything that happens in life whether it involves pleasure or pain. It’s a phrase that invokes a lifestyle of radical acceptance of the world in order to empower oneself into action every moment.
History and Etymology
A popular misconception is that “amor fati” is ancient Stoic motto, but the major Stoic philosophers like Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus wrote their works in ancient Greek. The ideas of Stoicism certainly played an influential role in the development of the term and concept, but it’s a far more modern invention.
The phrase was actually coined by Friedrich Nietzsche, who was likely inspired by Ralph Waldo Emerson’s beliefs about transcending external limitations by aligning one’s will to something independent of them, and Baruch Spinoza’s concept of “Amor intellectualis Dei,” which translates to “love of God or Nature” as a love for everything that happens in the universe as a necessary unfolding of its existence. Nietzsche, whose philological background exposed him to ancient Stoic metaphysics, derived a thought experiment called the Eternal Recurrence in which time is an infinite loop so that every person is bound to repeat every moment of their life for eternity. The only way Nietzsche could handle the existential anxiety of this idea, as he suffered from many physical health issues throughout his life, was to move beyond traditional Stoicism that focused on “tolerare,” or the enduring of hardship, and into an active love for the role suffering plays in life. To give meaning and even love to that suffering made the idea of repeating it forever more tolerable. He also sought to find empirical evidence for his thought experiment, eventually forming an argument relying on the Law of Thermodynamics to reason that a finite number of particles over an infinite amount of time would achieve and repeat every possible combination of their arrangements.
Nietzsche didn’t use the term often though. Robert Greene, a pop psych author, popularized the term in his books like The 48 Laws of Power (1998) and The 50th Law (2009) for high-powered ambitious individuals as a type of strategy for setbacks. Rather than processing the typical emotions around a problem or a defear, one could simply embrace it as something meant to happen for a reason in order to pivot into a new strategy. Ryan Holiday, a former research assistant for Greene, blurred the lines of its origin in his works like The Obstacle Is the Way (2014) and The Daily Stoic, tying “amor fati” directly to the lineage of Stoic writers like Aurelius and Epictetus. The Daily Stoic sells merchandise like brass medallions that are marked with “Amor Fati.”

wiki/amy-winehouse.title: Amy Winehouse
wiki/amy-winehouse.content:
Overview
Amy Winehouse was a widely celebrated English pop singer whose struggles with substance use were widely covered through the media. She died from alcohol poisoning after years of escalating mental health issues and rehab attempts following the death of her grandmother in 2005. She was hospitalized in 2007 for overdosing on a combination of heroin, cocaine, ketamine, alcohol, and MDMA (ecstacy). Although she had entered high levels of institutional care and undergone crisis interventions multiple times before, she was repeatedly resistant to formal psychiatric treatment and medication out of fear that it would dull her edge and creativity.

wiki/analgesia.title: Analgesia
wiki/analgesia.content:
Overview
Analgesics are compounds that relieve the experience of pain while maintaining consciousness. Anesthetics cause the loss of consciousness, so while anesthetics are routinely used in surgery, analgesics are used to address pain in a more ordinary daily context. Colloquially, analgesics are referred to as “painkillers,” and they can come in the form of opioids, NSAIDs, and acetaminophen so they have the potential to be addictive.

wiki/anhedonia.title: Anhedonia
wiki/anhedonia.content:
Overview
Anhedonia is the state of being unable to experience happiness or joy. This is in sometimes conflated with alexithymia, which is the inability to articulate the emotions someone might be experiencing. Someone with alexithymia might physically feel a fast heartbeat but not be aware if it’s fear or excitement. Someone with anhedonia doesn’t feel reward or pleasure when engaging with activities that ordinarily give people pleasure, like spending time with loved ones or eating their favorite food. It can be tied to depression or trauma, which means it can be temporary. In fact, in cases of severe depression, both can occur such that someone can neither experience happiness nor realize that they don’t experience happiness.

wiki/anorexia-nervosa.title: Anorexia Nervosa
wiki/anorexia-nervosa.content:
Overview
Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in which someone restricts their consumption of sustenance leading to a low enough body weight that health issues can arise. This can be a result of an extreme fear of gaining weight, often fueled by body dysmorphia in which someone can persistently feel overweight or in possession of too much fat even while presenting as skinny or seeing metrics establishing that they’re underweight. Anorexia has the second-highest death rate of any mental health condition, with the first being opioid overdose, as the malnutrition and mental distress associated with it can lead to fatal heart conditions and a high occurrence of suicide. It can also lead to a cessation in menstruation.
Much like substance use disorders, those with anorexia experience changes to their brain that make the disorder much more than just lifestyle choices or destabilizing insecurity. Studies show that people with anorexia have notable reductions in various parts of the brain that, and these reductions are two to four times larger than the variation of brain proportions found in individuals with other mental health conditions. This means a combination of physiological treatments and mental health interventions are deployed to address recovery from anorexia.
The most effective treatments known for adolescent anorexia involve family-based treatment (FBT), where 60% achieve full clinical remission as defined by achieving a healthy weight and normal eating patterns. Up to 87% at least achieve partial remission. This is twice as effective as individualized Adolescent-Focused Therapy (AFT). 75-90% of those who recovered through FBT maintained a healthy weight and, as applicable, regular menstruation long-term.
For adults, enhanced cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT-E) can have medium-to-large effects on reducing compulsive thoughts, restricting diet, and potential purging behaviors. Trials show that 60% of adults who undergo a 40-week protocol achieve substantial recovery; in a study evaluating virtual-first CBT-E, 50% of adults achieved at least 95% of their expected body weight. Specialist Supportive Clinical Management (SSCM) is an alternative approach that structures clinical exams, nutritional edu ation, and practical therapy focused on symptom management. The Maudsley Model of Anorexia Nervosa Treatment for Adults (MANTRA) is a specialized therapeutic interventions focused on cognitive and emotional aspects of one’s mind that sustain anorexia like perfectionism. Studies show that these approaches generally have similar effectiveness in long-term recovery outcomes.

wiki/anorexics-and-bulimics-anonymous.title: Anorexic and Bulimics Anonymous
wiki/anorexics-and-bulimics-anonymous.content:
Anorexic and Bulimics Anonymous (ABA) adapts the Twelve Step approach of AA for eating disorders.
Some studies find that 1 in 4 individuals diagnosed with an eating disorder will also develop a substance use disorder. Among adult women specifically with eating disorders, up to 50% report a history of substance abuse. Up to 35% of individuals with a substance use disorder also present with a co-occurring eating disorder. For context, that’s about 11 times higher the baseline of the general population.
It’s not so hard to see the connection between substances and appetite in general. Marijuana induces food cravings which can induce binge eating.  Depending on the person, alcohol can increase or decrease appetite. Chronic heavy drinking can have long-term impacts on appetite and nutritional absorption. Nicotine and caffeine are widely used as appetite suppressants, hence the “European breakfast” consisting of coffee and cigarettes. There’s evidence of business in the early industrial eras providing their workers with those to avoid raising wages to cover a real breakfast. It should be noted though that studies about the effectiveness of their appetite suppression are mixed, and each person’s body will react differently of course. And by no means should you actually pick this up as a habit to lose weight, it’s not safe.
It should go without saying, but I’ll say it anyways: nothing on this site constitutes medical advice or should be seen as a substitute for consulting a medical professional. I’m just some dude looking at studies from actual experts. I do feel confident though in saying that you should not skip meals in favor of drugs.
From my understanding, at the level of peer support groups and recovery programs, treating the compulsive thoughts associated with eating disorders similarly to the cravings associated with addiction is a solid approach. Those with co-occurring disorders can apply recovery philosophies and tools throughout their lives, such as dealing with overlapping triggers at once.
On the other hand, unlike substances or many process addictions, no one can achieve complete abstinence from eating, so modified programs frame the issue as abstinence from the behaviors associated with their eating disorders.
Plus, while many recovering from substances do face nutritional imbalances, many in recovery tend to feel better simply through supplements and a restored appetite. That isn’t to say there isn’t a whole field and industry around remedying the ways substances interfere with nutritional absorption or deficits. However, for those with eating disorders, it’s far more likely that they will need medical professionals to assess physical complications that can stem from eating disorders. Starvation and purging cause different metabolic changes than chronic substance abuse, though both are real and serious. An alcoholic who hasn’t eaten a real meal in weeks might struggle to regain hold down food and return to their baseline appetite, but severely malnourished patients who attempt to return to baseline appetite can trigger fatal events. There are tragic stories you may have heard about Holocaust survivors who died from eating and drinking too quickly after being freed.
When the body begins to receive nourishment, it releases a surge of insulin that can drive essential minerals out of the bloodstream and into cells, triggering heart failures, respiratory arrest, and seizures. Sudden fluid shifts that produce electrolyte imbalances can trigger cardiac arrythmias in heart muscles that were weakened as they were broken down for energy. Stomach muscles that are responsible for pushing food through the intestines also atrophy, so eating can cause intense nausea and pain. I could keep going on, but I hope the point comes across: eating disorders require unique medical interventions from experts who know exactly how to calibrate meals and fluid ingestion, sometimes intravenously.
I’ve also been generalizing “eating disorders” as one group when they have extremely different characteristics. Anorexia nervosa can involve compulsions like addiction, but binge eating mimics substance use much closer since the body receives signals from the food as an external source.
Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID)
ARFID is an eating disorder that was introduced into the DSM-5 in 2013 where someone limits their food intake for reasons unrelated to body image or weight. Rather than anorexia or bulimia, it results from sensory sensitivity, past trauma, and a low drive to eat. To meet the criteria, there must be weight loss, nutritional deficiencies, dependence on tube feeding or nutritional supplements, and interference with regular social activities.
Eating Disorders in Men
There are countless women who have spoken about eating disorders and how it has affected their lives, and how systemic sexism in every layer of society plays a role in reinforcing harmful body standards. This section is not in any way intended to detract or denigrate their perspectives or the real data researchers have collected behind these standards. I only started with this section before Eating Disorders in Women because I’m a little more equipped to speak on standards of men.
While women are more likely to develop eating disorders than men, and that speaks to social gendered standards we all internalize, men still represent roughly 1 in 3 cases of eating disorders.
There are some notable differences in presentations, such as men being more likely to use excessive and compulsive exercise to compensate for calories while women are more likely to induce vomiting and abuse laxatives. Exercise can be a process addiction itself too, and one that many substance addicts can switch into in early recovery as a seemingly healthier substitute, but all things can be used in excess as an unhealthy crutch.
Also, men are less likely to be screened or seek help for eating disorders due to the assumption that it only impacts women, so when they do receive treatment, they tend to have more severe complications. Men who identify as LGBTQ+ are significantly more likely to experience issues with body image and eating disorders.
From 2000 to 2018, the prevalence of eating disorders across the world doubled and seems to continue rising, with men experiencing a faster growth rate than women. The post-pandemic tracking shows that the ratio of male-to-female cases has gone from 1:10 to 1:5 acccording to post-COVID pandemic data. The increase seems concentrated among 10 to 14 year old girls, but also 20 to 24 year old adults regardless of gender identification. Under the ARFID diagnostic category, we see a roughly equal gender split among the 6% of 10 year olds who meet the criteria.
Unquestionably, social media is

shower

Eating Disorders as Addictions
I’ll admit, I have little exposure to anything about eating disorders aside from what has been confided in me privately by people I’ve met. This section will thus rely heavily on what I found in the literature.
The general concept of disordered eating patterns is as old as the concept of habitual drunkenness, which is to say that you can find descriptions matching the disorders as far back as ancient Greece. Psychiatry as we know it emerged in the last couple centuries.
In 1868, Sir William Withey Gull, a doctor for Queen Victoria of England, observed a pattern of weight loss, cessation of regular periods, and dangerously low heart rates in young women that didn’t seem to result from any physical illness. In 1973, he used “anorexia nervosa” to mean a “nervous lack of appetite” and pointed towards a mental origin. The treatments he recommended involved removing patients from their old environments and implementing strict feeding schedules regardless of the patient’s appetite.
The term “eating addiction” was used in the 1930s to describe patients with patterns of binge eating. In the 1950s, the term “food addiction” was used. By the 60s and 70s, eating disorders were examined as their own psychiatric conditions beyond neurotic symptoms. In 1979, Gerald Russell

wiki/answerability.title: Answerability
wiki/answerability.content:
Overview
Answerability in philosophical discourse refers to the responsibility an agent has in providing rational justifications for their actions. For instance, an animal can’t articulate a reason for its actions, so even though we can attribute actions to it and deliver consequences as a form of accountability to learn from, so it might not make sense to assign moral responsibility to it. Similarly, a toddler can’t provide a moral justification or reason for their actions as they lack the cognitive ability to consider abstract ethical principles, even if they can understand agency and consequences. Of course, there are plenty of grey areas and subjective evaluations when we apply this to adults who have at some point had the capacity to evaluate ethical principles.

wiki/antagonist.title: Antagonist
wiki/antagonist.content:
Overview
Antagonists are substances that block or reduce the body’s biological response by binding to cell receptors to stop other chemicals from binding to it, applicable to both natural chemicals produced by the body as well as external chemicals called agonists. In some cases, antagonists can displace chemicals already in the body to prevent ongoing reactions. Beta-blockers are a form of antagonists that block adrenaline from increasing blood pressure and straining the heart. Antihistamines, as the name suggests, block histamine receptors to reduce the itching and swelling that accompany allergic reactions.
Naloxone, or narcan, is one of the most critical antagonists used to prevent overdoses by instantaneously blocking opioid receptors.

wiki/anterior-cingulate-cortex.title: Anterior Cingulate Cortex (ACC)
wiki/anterior-cingulate-cortex.content:
Overview
The anterior cingulate cortext (ACC) is a part of the brain involved in decision-making, reward anticipation, and impulse control, all of which factor into substance use disorders. After chronic substance use, the gray matter involved in detecting harmful decisions can atrophy while the regions that process negative emotions can become hyperactive. The combination leads to difficulty in associating the choice to use a substance with harm while also feeling strong urges to seek relief to strong negative emotions. The neurotransmitter glutamate is used to communicate with the striatum that facilitates habit-formation through reward processing, and chronic substance use disrupts the glutamate receptors so that the habits associated with compulsive substance use solidify. When processing a substance, the ACC is hyperactivated, and when resisting compulsions to use again, the ACC is hypoactivated. Over time, the ACC reassigns salience, or the perceived significance, from natural survival needs and long-term goals to addictive substances or processes that provide a strong reward.

wiki/antidepressants.title: Antidepressants
wiki/antidepressants.content:
Overview
Antidepressants are a class of medications that target the production of monoamine neurotransmitters like serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine which are thought to be associated with depression and anxiety.
The old biological theory of depression posits that an imbalance between these is responsible for depression, and this is still the narrative commonly found in the public consciousness thanks to pharmaceutical marketing campaigns, but the consensus in research circles is that reality is more complex. Consider that if you take aspirin to address a headache, we wouldn’t necessarily say you had an aspirin-deficiency. Yet, this was the assumption made by researchers and clinicians upon observing that providing patients with drugs that boosted their serotonin levels also improved their symptoms of depression. In 2022, a study led by Joanna Moncrieff at University College London analyzed decades of data and found no consistent evidence that low serotonin levels were the cause of depression.
Instead, modern research is interested in neuroplasticity and neurogenesis as explanations. The inflammation and floods of cortisol from chronic stress is thought to drop a protein called Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) which stimulates the repair and rebuilding of neural pathway. Antidepressants might work by increasing the activity of BDNF over the course of weeks or months; this means that they can increase neuroplasticty, but not that they automatically provide feelings of happiness without a psychosocial framework that takes advantage of the brain’s capacity to change.

wiki/antisocial.title: Antisocial
wiki/antisocial.content:
Overview
“Antisocial” in the context of psychology and psychiatry refers to a pattern of disregard for the rights and wellbeing of others. While it might be used casually to refer to introverted dispositions or self-isolating behavior, the [[diagnostic-and-statistical-manual-of-mental-disorders|Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders]] lays out specific criteria for Antisocial Personality Disorder that manifest before the age of 15 outside of episodic co-occurring disorders:


Failure to conform to social norms and lawful behaviors


Deceitfulness through lying for personal gain


Impulsivity or failure to plan ahead


Irritability & Aggressiveness including physical assaults


Reckless disregard for safety for oneself or others


Consistent irresponsibility such as a failure to maintain a work ethic or meet agreed-upon obligations


lack of remorse through indifference or rationalization


Individuals diagnosed with ASPD are almost 8 times more likely to develop substance use disorders as the general population, though this shouldn’t be taken to mean that most people with substance use disorders have antisocial personality traits. Instead, psychologists consider that someone with ASPD and substance dependence are both part of an externalizing spectrum of vulnerabilities around behavioral control. Those on the externalizing spectrum are more likely to express their negative feelings outwardly through actions rather than inwardly through depression or anxiety. Both disorders are connected to impaired or reduced activity in the prefrontal cortext that’s responsible for judgment and self-control, which then amplifies short-term rewards over long-term consequences. They’re also related through low serotonin levels that fuel irritability and impulsivity that can drive a desire for instant relief despite consequences. ASPD often features a low baseline for emotional activation that presents as boredom or feelings of emptiness.
A 2012 twin study found that the genetic risks of ASPD have two dimensions:


disinhibition factor: this measures a genetic predisposition towards impulsivity and novely-seeking behaviors that heavily overlaps with substance use disorders


agressive-disregard factor: this measures a genetic predisposition towards irritability and a lack of empathy that can result in physical outbursts


Other twin studies find that the factors involved in the causes of antisocial behaviors shift dramatically based on age. When under 15, twins experiencing juvenile delinquency show that shared environments through family dynamics, community trauma, and socioeconomic status play a big role in the behaviors that meet the ASPD criteria. In early adulthood however, the influence of shared family environments declines almost entirely while genetic factors and environmental factors such as specific trauma or peer groups are seen as more dominant drivers. In short, we might expect teens to act out impulsively and destructively in response to a traumatic environment, but whether that baseline continues into adulthood depends a lot on genetic factors and individual trauma. It has similar heritability to conditions like bipolar disorder and schizophrenia.
Commentary
Frank Cotton, The Hellbound Heart
[[the-hellbound-heart|The Hellbound Heart]] by Clive Barker can be interpreted as a depiction of an extreme case of unmanaged ASPD told through the lens of Gothic transgression. I’ve elsewhere given an interpretation of the character of Frank Cotton that compares his desire to experience something transcendental beyond what normal earthly sensations can provide to compulsive substance use to experience any change at all to in intolerable present state. Frank can also be seen as a stereotypical case of ASPD, as we find out that, unlike his twin brother, even as a teenager he lacked the baseline rewards from ordinary life, which compelled him to try riskier and more hedonistic options to feel something. At the same time, there’s a strong stigma attached to ASPD that can deter individuals with it from seeking treatment to the benefit of both themselves and the society they are antisocial within. Cognitive therapies addressing ASPD often reframe an individual’s approach rather than their desires, so even though they may have the desire to do something illegal for personal gain, they can pause and reason that other legitimate avenues to personal gain can be more sustainable. It appeals to rational self-interest rather than attempting to frame a disregard for others as a cognitive distortion to be challenged. With characters like Frank, it can be easy to dismiss those with ASPD as born rotten, especially when heritability studies are interpreted to mean someone was doomed to be destructive rather than at-risk.

wiki/antitoxic.title: Antitoxic
wiki/antitoxic.content:
Overview
“Antitoxic” refers to compounds and processes that act to neutralize something identified as toxic.
History and Etymology
In the early 1900s, physicians like George Pettey and Ernest Bishop argued that chronic substance use should be studied as:
“A disease, a toxemia, of drug, auto- and intestinal origin, the management and treatment of which belong to the field of internal medicine and not to neurology. The vital and essential principle of the treatment advocated is elimination.”

wiki/anxiety-and-depression-association-.title: Anxiety and Depression Association of America Peer-to-Peer Communities
wiki/anxiety-and-depression-association-.content:
Founded in 1980, the Anxiety and Depression Association of America is a nonprofit organization in Silver Spring, Maryland. They function as an educational and research organization that advocates for addressing anxiety, depression, and other related disorders. They also maintain online peer communities for anxiety and depression through a partnership with HealthUnlocked, a social media network centered on health operated by PPD Inc, which is a subsidiary of Thermo Fisher Scientific: healthunlocked.com/anxiety-depression-support
As of the writing of this sentence, there are 106,455 members and 97,968 posts, with more added every few hours.
Note that posts are still indexed by search engines, so consider how much you value anonymity before participating. Medical information isn’t just more personally sensitive than your Instagram pics, it can also function as an identifier like a fingerprint if you describe the same set of symptoms in the same way. They also collect some data for research and collaboration with private partners, including pharmaceutical organizations.
I haven’t found any controversies online about HealthUnlocked or the ADAA peer communities specifically, but it would be prudent to apply the same precautions you would if you were trying to be anonymous on any other platform.
Remember that unverifiable anecdotes shouldn’t be taken as certain facts, all online communities can become echo chambers that either confirm your biases or judge without knowing the details of your life, every single database can be hacked or leaked, and no online site’s service should be interpreted as medical advice that substitutes for the opinions of healthcare professionals.
Links
adaa.org/find-help/support

wiki/anxiety.title: Anxiety
wiki/anxiety.content:
Overview
The American Psychological Association defines anxiety as “an emotion characterized by apprehension and somatic symptoms of tension in which an individual anticipates impending danger, catastrophe, or misfortune. The body often mobilizes itself to meet the perceived threat: Muscles become tense, breathing is faster, and the heart beats more rapidly.”
When used as a casual shorthand, anxiety is often interchangeable with fear in general or Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), in which someone experiences chronic and uncontrollable anxiety across multiple areas of life that lasts longer than six months in ways that disrupt daily life. However, the two cases are very distinct; anxiety as an emotion is considered a normal response to specific stressful event like a public speaking obligation, but generalized anxiety involves chronic worry about a wide variety of things without a specific stressor. GAD also comes with distinct physical sypmtoms like restlessness, frequent or constant fatigue, muscle aches and headaches, and trouble sleeping.
Links

www.apa.org/topics/anxiety

wiki/anxious-attachment.title: Anxious Attachment
wiki/anxious-attachment.content:
Overview
Anxious attachment is a type of attachment style in developmental and relational psychology that’s characterized by deep fears of rejection or abandonment. This can result in seeking constant validation or reassurance in the desire for close intimacy, observed through overthinking, people-pleasing, low self-esteem, and “clingy” behaviors. Anxious attachment styles are often thought to develop out of inconsistent or unpredictable attitudes from caregivers in childhood. Children who observe sudden swings between warm and cold treatment from their parents or guardians can end up insecure in their attachments without constant temperature checks.

wiki/apatheia.title: Apatheia
wiki/apatheia.content:
Overview
“Apatheia” is a term that originates from ancient Greek Stoic philosophy in which one’s state of mind is undisturbed by passionate temptations. While the current term “apathy” seems derived from “apatheia”, “apathy” has a connotation centered around negative indifference while “apatheia” is closer to stability and composure.

wiki/applied-behavior-analysis.title: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)
wiki/applied-behavior-analysis.content:
Overview
Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is a discipline that studies the way behaviors are learned and reinforced by one’s environment, especially as a form of therapy. It’s commonly used with developmental disorders or autism spectrum disorder (ASD) as an evidence-backed modality that involves positive reinforcement to reward desired behaviors while reducing undesirable ones.
A core model for ABA is the ABC model that tracks an Antecedent (what happens before the behavior), Behavior, and Consequence (what happens after the behavior). This lends itself easily using data to drive and evaluate the reinforcement patterns. Specific protocols include:


Discrete Trial Training (DTT)


Pivotal Response Treatment (PRT)


Early Start Denver Model (ESDM)


Functional Behavior Assessment (FBA)


In the United States, ABA practitioners must have credentials achieved through the Behavioral Analyst Certification Board (BACB). Generally, these practitioners tend to be:


Registered Behavior Technician


Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst (BCaBA)


Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA)

wiki/armchair-expert.title: Armchair Expert
wiki/armchair-expert.content:
Overview
An armchair expert is someone who has no training or experience in a particular subject but provides commentary or critique as if one does. It’s why I try to emphasize that I have no inherent qualification that makes me better than anyone else at interpreting the evidence I look like, and I characterize my work as a series of amateur and opinionated literature surveys.

wiki/asads-conference.title: ASADS Conference
wiki/asads-conference.content:
Overview
The Alabama School of Alcohol and Other Drug Studies was established in 1974 after the Hughes Act (1970) gave states federal funding to address alcohol abuse. Although Alabama now had these funds, the state lacked a workforce trained to handle substance use disorders. Rather than providing manuals or academic-style coursework, the event created multi-day learning tracks to quickly get caught up on the latest trends in addiction studies, prevention science, and best practices for co-occurring mental health disorders.
They also present the Carl Nowell Leadership Award to individuals in Alabama who demonstrated exceptional leadership and collaboration in addressing addiction through prevention, treatment, and/or recovery.
Attendees


Maurice Clarett, former Ohio State football player


David Bartley


Tim Lupinacci, CEO of Baker Donelson


Marc Fomby, CEO of FTC Prevention Services


Links

asadsonline.com/

wiki/asam-presidential-award.title: Presidential Award | ASAM
wiki/asam-presidential-award.content:
Summary
According to the homepage:
“The ASAM Presidential Award honors an individual for outstanding dedication and service in addressing addiction issues or promoting education, training or awareness of the specialty of addiction medicine.”
The award’s name comes from its selection process, which consists entirely of the discretion of the ASAM President.  From the 2026 press release announcing the winner:
“ASAM President Stephen Taylor, MD, MPH, DFAPA, DFASAM, has selected Dr. Athanasiou for this honor in 2026. Dr. Athanasiou is a supervising mental health psychiatrist with the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health and a health sciences associate clinical professor with the Department of Psychiatry at UCLA. As chair of the ASAM Publications Council and editor in chief of The ASAM Weekly, he has helped keep addiction medicine audiences informed of the latest commentary, news, and research shaping the field”
Because the award is applied at the President’s discretion, there are years where Presidents decline to grant the award to anyone. For example, Brian Hurley, the ASAM President during the 2024 and 2025 award processes, declined to grant it to anyone.
Winners


Nicholas Athanasiou (2026)


Anthony P. Albanese (2023): worked to expand health training positions within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) with an emphasis on shifting to a Whole Health model of car and serving veterans struggling with chronic pain in rural areas. Albanese is also a professor within the University of California system ( Davis). The ASAM President at the time was William F. Haning III.


Mark R. Publicker (2021)


Nora D. Volkow (2019)


Sharon L. Stancliff (2018)


Arlene C. Deverman (2017)


Governor Larry Hogan (2016)


Alexis Geier-Horan (2015)


Bonnie Wilford (2012)


Jag H. Khalsa (2011)


Claire Osman (2010)
